Organizing? Oh, man, it's a disaster. It used to be fine when I was at my old job because we had this really rigid ticketing system and an escalation calendar. It basically told me what to do and when to do it. But now? Without that structure, my days just turn into these massive piles of sticky notes. I've got half-finished emails, reminders for my chess club, orders for computer parts... it's just a mess. 

Speaking of parts, I actually ordered this new solid-state drive last week. A 2-terabyte NVMe M.2 drive. The read/write speeds on those things are just insane compared to the old SATA drives. I remember when I bought my first hard drive back in the 90s, it was, like, 500 megabytes and cost a fortune. It was the size of a brick. I tried explaining that to my nephew the other day—he's super into building gaming PCs now, all RGB lights and water cooling. He's got this whole setup with dual monitors and a streaming camera. Kids these days don't know how good they have it. When I was his age, if you wanted to play a multiplayer game, you had to physically carry your tower to a buddy's house for a LAN party. We used to stay up until 4 AM playing Doom, drinking Mountain Dew until our teeth hurt. The network setup for those LAN parties was a nightmare, though. Coaxial cables everywhere, terminators at the ends... if one person tripped over a wire, the whole network went down. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my daily tasks. Yeah, so without the old system, I honestly can't tell what has to happen first. Everything just blends together, and I don't realize something is a priority until it's already overdue and someone is yelling at me about it.

Change my routine? I mean... I don't know if I've really *changed* anything on purpose, you know? It's more like my routine just kind of dissolved. I guess I haven't really made any major lifestyle shifts specifically because of the focus stuff or the fidgeting. It's just that everything takes twice as long now, so my whole day gets eaten up. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to be setting up a mesh network for a client. Mesh networks are fantastic, by the way. Way better than just using a single router with a bunch of cheap range extenders. The handoff between nodes is completely seamless. You can walk from the kitchen to the garage and your Zoom call won't drop once. I always recommend the Wi-Fi 6E systems now because the 6GHz band is practically empty in most neighborhoods. It's like having a private highway for your data. I was explaining this to the guy at Best Buy last week because he was trying to sell this elderly couple a $400 gaming router they definitely didn't need. They just wanted to FaceTime their grandkids! I had to step in. I can't stand when salespeople take advantage of people who don't know tech. I ended up talking to them for like forty-five minutes in the router aisle. The husband used to work for IBM back in the mainframe days. He was telling me about these massive tape drives they used to use...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask if I changed my routine? Yeah, no, I haven't really changed my lifestyle or anything to deal with it. I'm just kind of... surviving the chaos, I guess.

We used to do it all the time with the old Celeron 300A chips back in the late 90s. You could bump the front-side bus from 66 megahertz to 100, and suddenly you had a 450-megahertz processor for a fraction of the cost of a Pentium II. It was the golden age of PC building. You just had to make sure you had a massive heatsink and a really loud fan, or the whole thing would literally fry. I had this one setup in a custom acrylic case, with neon cold cathode tubes inside. We'd stay up until 4 AM playing Quake III Arena and drinking Bawls energy drink. Do they still make that stuff? It came in these really cool blue glass bottles with little bumps all over them.
